Menelaus. King of Sparta and husband of Helen, he was the nominal cause of the Trojan War when the Trojan prince Paris abducted his wife. Though less prominent than his brother Agamemnon or the great Achilles in the actual fighting, Menelaus remained a capable warrior and ultimately stood as the war's victor. He co-led the Greek forces alongside his brother from Sparta, helping to coordinate the thousand-ship invasion. In the Iliad, he challenged Paris to single combat to resolve their dispute, though that duel was interrupted before it could conclude. Despite lacking the superhuman martial prowess of Achilles and other legendary Greek heroes, Menelaus fought alongside Nestor and other Greek leaders and survived the entire ten-year conflict. After Troy's fall, he famously retrieved Helen and with her returned home, though their reunion was complicated and marked by lingering tension. He appears in Homer's Odyssey as a successful returning home, protected by the gods and honored as a war victor. He took an active role in the funeral games held for Ajax and in distributing the war prizes among the Greeks, fulfilling his duties as one of the war's leaders.
